Add or update one source translation key and translate it into the target locales.

## Synopsis

```bash
the-i18n-cli translate-key --layer <layer> --key <key> --sourceLocale <sourceLocale>
```

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--layer` | `string` | yes | — | Layer holding the key, from discover (e.g., "root", "app-admin"). |
| `--key` | `string` | yes | — | Dot-separated key path to translate. Example: "bookingCreator.options.removeSubResource". |
| `--sourceLocale` | `string` | yes | — | Source locale ref. May be a code ("en-us"), a language ("en-US") or a file ("en-US.json"). |
| `--sourceValue` | `string` | no | — | Source value to write before translating. If omitted, the existing source value is read. |
| `--targetLocales`, `--targets` | `string` | no | — | Locales to translate into. Pass "all", or omit, for every locale except the source. Comma-separated, or "all". |
| `--overwrite` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Overwrite existing target translations. When false, only missing targets are filled. Default: true. |
| `--dryRun` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Report the source and target locales without writing files or calling the translation backend. Default: false. |
| `--includePreview` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Include the translated values in the result. Default: false, which keeps the response compact. |
| `--provider=<openai\|anthropic\|google>` | `string` | no | — | LLM provider to translate through. Without one nothing is translated automatically — the result carries the contexts to translate by hand instead. |
| `--model` | `string` | no | — | Model name. Required whenever a provider is set. |
| `--apiKey` | `string` | no | — | API key. Falls back to the OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY environment variables. |
| `--baseUrl` | `string` | no | — | Provider base URL for gateways, self-hosted models and proxies speaking the provider's protocol. Falls back to I18N_BASE_URL, then to providerBaseUrl in .i18n-mcp.json. |

Every command accepts the [shared flags](/reference/cli#shared-flags) and sets one of the [exit codes](/reference/cli#exit-codes) documented on the overview.
